source: Kanagaraj V., Asaithambi G., Toledo T., Lee T.-C. (2015), Trajectory data and flow characteristics of mixed traffic, Transportation Research Record 2491, 1-11. Chennai, 2:45-3:15 PM, 0.5 s sampling. Processed by weave_data (positions only).

lengthM.note: Constant in the dataset (1 distinct value(s) over 1695 vehicles; mode 1.8 m): a fixed size assigned by the data producers, not a measurement.

widthM.note: Constant in the dataset (1 distinct value(s) over 1695 vehicles; mode 0.6 m): a fixed size assigned by the data producers, not a measurement.

v0.note: 85th percentile of position-derived spot speeds at x=138.1 m (1491 vehicles). Traffic is near capacity (~41 km/h), so free-flow vehicles are rare: a proxy for the desired speed, likely an underestimate.

T.note: Median of T = (s·sqrt(1-(v/v0)^4) - s0)/v over 2261 steady-following samples (|a|<0.25 m/s², |Δv|<0.5 m/s, v≥3.0 m/s, gap≤60 m; leader by the engine rule). CONDITIONAL on the assumed s0=2 m and the proxy v0=14.62 m/s: T ranges 0.52-0.81 s under s0±1 m, v0±10%. 312 of 2573 steady samples (12.1%) with v > 0.9·v0 were excluded before inverting.

s0.note: Literature default: Treiber & Kesting (2013), Traffic Flow Dynamics, Table 11.2, IDM s0 = 2 m (city traffic). The data has almost no slow or stopped following, so s0 is not identifiable.

a.note: Informed by position-derived acceleration percentiles (p95 of 54470 clean samples), but the value is set by the smoothing window (9-point = 4 s quadratic Savitzky–Golay): 5 pts 3.73, 7 pts 2.03, 9 pts 1.25, 11 pts 0.87, 15 pts 0.50 m/s² (see VALIDATION.md). Never the dataset's acceleration column.

b.note: Informed by position-derived acceleration percentiles (minus p5 of 54470 clean samples), but the value is set by the smoothing window (9-point SG): 5 pts 3.80, 7 pts 2.09, 9 pts 1.33, 11 pts 0.96, 15 pts 0.58 m/s² (see VALIDATION.md). Never the dataset's acceleration column.

c0.note: p10 of accepted lateral gaps to side-by-side neighbours, halved (c = gap/2: the engine adds c on both sides). 24768 gap samples involving this class; c at p5/p10/p15 = 0.226/0.333/0.412 m; median gap 1.98 m (not used).

c1.note: Speed slope not identified (slope not distinguishable from 0 (|b| ≤ 2 SE)); set to 0.

criticalS.note: Not identified by the Chennai data (mid-block section, no priority conflicts). HCM 2016 (TRB) two-way-stop base values 4.1 s critical / 2.2 s follow-up; two-wheelers/autos in Indian traffic are reported to accept shorter gaps; not quantified here. Editable assumption.

maxSpeedMps.note: Peak |lateral speed| of deliberate lateral moves: episodes = monotonic lateral displacement ≥ 1 m on 5-point SG smoothed position, reversals below the hysteresis 0.056 m (4·√2·σ_s, σ_y = 0.014 m) ignored, split at pauses ≥ 2 s with |vy| < 0.036 m/s; speed by 3-point central difference (noise sd 0.020 m/s). Only fully observed moves are used (user decision): a partly observed move's measured peak can only be at or below its true peak, so including them should lower p85; that it raises p85 instead points to smoothing artefacts at stretch/trajectory ends (26% of the 1690 partly observed peaks lie within 2 samples of a stretch end). p85 of n = 552 episode peaks (p75/p95 = 0.74/1.12 m/s); 3.5 m at this speed takes 4.1 s. Previously 0.57 m/s (p95 over all samples, mostly drift).

politeness.note: MOBIL politeness, lower end of the typical range in Kesting, Treiber & Helbing (2007), Transp. Res. Rec. 1999.

thresholdMps2.note: MOBIL switching threshold 0.1 m/s² (Kesting, Treiber & Helbing 2007).
